subject.title: Bug: Poe image/video-output models are accepted in config but fail at runtime (Nano Banana 400, Veo/Sora fallback)

question: Should OpenClaw reject media-output provider model refs in chat/session runtime with a clear diagnostic, or add first-class output-modality metadata that routes them through media generation?
rationale: Both choices change public provider/model semantics: diagnostic-first needs a reliable way to identify output-only models, while first-class support requires broader provider, tool, response, and channel contracts.

options.title: Diagnostic-first contract
options.body: Treat media-output models as unsupported chat/session models for now, add clear errors and docs, and leave generation on image_generate/video_generate.

options.title: First-class media-output models
options.body: Add output modality metadata and route image/video-output refs through media generation with channel delivery support.

options.title: Defer to provider plugins
options.body: Keep core behavior unchanged until a Poe or generic media provider plugin proves the missing API surface.

recommendation.title: Diagnostic-first contract
recommendation.body: Treat media-output models as unsupported chat/session models for now, add clear errors and docs, and leave generation on image_generate/video_generate.

likelyOwner.reason: The input-modality preservation work and adjacent provider/config history make this the best available owner signal for deciding the next public contract.
